findings.statement: CA9 is the top convergence gene: RNA is up in tumour [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=6.312], protein confirms it [gene=CA9; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.269], and TCGA-KIRC replicates [gene=CA9; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=9.712]. Caveat: GTEx vital-organ proteome shows stomach enrichment [gene=CA9; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=5.19], an on-target off-tumour consideration; it is not prognostic in TCGA.

CD70 is a membrane target with protein up in tumour [gene=CD70; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.421], replicated in TCGA [gene=CD70; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=7.09], and with low tissue specificity in vital organs [gene=CD70; type=normal_proteome; source=DATASET:GTEX-PROTEOME; vital_protein_ts_max=0.34], a favourable safety signal. Antibody-based agents (cusatuzumab, vorsetuzumab) exist; the gene is tumour-intrinsic after purity extrapolation.

ENPP3, a surface enzyme with an antibody-drug conjugate in clinical development (AGS-16C3F, phase 2), is up at protein level [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.544] and RNA [gene=ENPP3; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=3.895], with a tumour-intrinsic purity signal.

SCARB1 ranks first in the target profile: protein up [gene=SCARB1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=1.837] and RNA up [gene=SCARB1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=2.974], tumour-intrinsic and replicated in TCGA; it has no clinical-stage drug in the graph and is not a DepMap dependency, so it is a lipid-uptake hypothesis rather than a validated target.

NNMT is strongly up at protein [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=2.709] and RNA [gene=NNMT; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-RNA; layer=rna; log2fc=4.67], tumour-intrinsic, and higher expression predicts worse survival in TCGA [gene=NNMT; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.301]. It is the best-scoring gene in the biomarker profile among up-regulated genes.

SLC16A3 (MCT4, lactate exporter and a HIF-driven glycolysis gene) is up in TCGA-KIRC [gene=SLC16A3; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=3.291], and is a tumour-intrinsic, druggable membrane transporter in the target profile.

VHL is the disease driver: recurrently mutated [gene=VHL; type=somatic_recurrence; source=DATASET:SOMATIC-CPTAC-TCGA; freq=48.34%] and lost with its 3p arm [gene=VHL; type=omics_cnv; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-CNV; arm=3p; loss_freq=79.1%], with a positive cis copy-number effect on RNA. Loss drives the HIF-target signature (CA9, NNMT, ANGPTL4, SLC16A3 and others); it is mechanism, not a direct drug target.

PSAT1 is the top biomarker-profile gene and is down in tumour at protein [gene=PSAT1; type=omics_de; source=DATASET:CPTAC-CCRCC-PROTEOME; layer=protein; log2fc=-1.963]; in TCGA, high expression predicts worse survival [gene=PSAT1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=0.43]. Direction is down, so this is a prognostic tissue biomarker, not a target.

ALDOB, a proximal-tubule identity gene, is lost in tumour in TCGA [gene=ALDOB; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=-4.741], and higher expression is associated with better survival [gene=ALDOB; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.358]. It reflects loss of normal tubule identity, so it is a diagnostic/prognostic biomarker rather than a target.

PCK1 (gluconeogenesis, proximal tubule) is down in tumour and ranks second in the biomarker profile; higher expression associates with better survival in TCGA [gene=PCK1; type=tcga_survival; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log_hr_per_sd=-0.415], consistent with metabolic de-differentiation tracking aggressiveness.

UMOD, a thick ascending limb marker, shows one of the largest tumour-versus-normal drops in TCGA [gene=UMOD; type=tcga_de; source=DATASET:TCGA-KIRC-RNA; log2fc=-13.139]; it is a normal-nephron identity marker (tissue-of-origin/diagnostic) with no therapeutic rationale, and it is not prognostic.

caveats: Rankings are deterministic score integrations; high rank is not clinical validation.
Down-regulated tubule genes (ALDOB, UMOD, PCK1) reflect loss of normal cell identity and partly composition differences between tumour and adjacent normal.
CA9 shows stomach enrichment in the GTEx vital-organ proteome (kidney is absent from that proteome), so safety of CA9-directed agents needs checking.
DepMap and PRISM 2D cell-line layers miss HIF-2 biology; no target here is a selective ccRCC dependency in DepMap.
I did not run phosphosite, kinase-activity or per-gene purity calls separately; purity, cis-copy-number and tractability statements come from the convergence_ranking components.
Several statements about drugs (cusatuzumab, AGS-16C3F) come from the graph's drug annotations, and the SLC16A3 and ENPP3 survival and DepMap results were not examined individually.
